transcript:
HEADER: Date: 2025-02-21 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration approx 58m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Tidewater CISO), Evan Cole (Compliance), Sonal Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey folks good afternoon, thanks for joining. Rana -- sorry i mean Marta -- earlier intro but nice to meet you all. We'll walk through our trust center artifacts and then priya will do a quick KMS/ops deep dive.
[00:18] Marta Ruiz: Thanks Jordan. We have about an hour. Primary ask is to understand what artifacts Redwood will provide for our SOC 2 and ISO mapping, and how evidence collection works, especially for keys and logs.
[00:31] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick agenda: Trust Center, SOC2/ISO certs and reports, controls mapping spreadsheet format, KMS and encryption, SSO/RBAC, logging/retention, Q&A, then next steps. Any additions?
[00:44] Evan Cole: Also want to confirm timelines for receiving the Type II report and whether there are bridge letters if our audit window doesn't align.
[00:52] Priya Nair: We'll cover attestation cadence and what we can provide — snapshots, console screenshots, and long term retention samples.

[05:12] Sonal Patel: Quick infra note — we need to know if Redwood's hosted offering keeps any PII in logs by default, and whether we can restrict to US-only regions.
[05:29] Priya Nair: Short answer: data residency is configurable for hosted customers; we have region pinning and dedicated options for strict requirements. On logs, default operational logs don't persist customer prompt content but audit logs of API calls (headers, request IDs) can be provided and retention can be configured. I'll pull the exact retention windows from the trust center.

[09:03] Jordan Lee: For trust center access, we'll send a temporary read-only link to the folder that contains our SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert, penetration test summary (redacted), and our controls mapping template. That's the usual approach.
[09:18] Marta Ruiz: Do you provide SOC 2 bridge letters? Our audit wraps in March, customer audit is in May, we may need the bridge.
[09:25] Jordan Lee: We can provide a bridge letter in some cases — depends on the auditor and scope. We'll include what we've done historically and coordinate with your audit contact.

[12:02] Evan Cole: About the controls mapping, is there a canonical mapping to SOC 2 CC categories and ISO controls? We need a CSV we can hand to our audit team.
[12:14] Priya Nair: Yes we have a controls spreadsheet. It maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001 clauses and lists sample evidence artifacts (console screenshot, log export, policy doc link). We'll share the template.

[16:40] Marta Ruiz: KMS question — do you manage keys for hosted customers? Is customer-managed keys via HSM supported? And what's the key rotation policy?
[16:53] Priya Nair: Hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys by default (KMS provider: AWS KMS in our current regions). For enterprise/private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM-backed keys; you can supply rotation policies. Rotation is supported and we log key usage in audit trails.
[17:10] Sonal Patel: If we bring our own key, can Redwood still do re-encryption for cached KV entries?
[17:20] Priya Nair: Yes, but there are operational caveats around rekeying and KV cache TTL. We'll demo this in the KMS deep-dive. There was some confusion earlier in docs where kv cache was transcribed as K V cash in one doc — apologies for the weird wording.

[22:01] Jordan Lee: On RBAC and SSO: we support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning for user and group sync. Role matrix is configurable via admin console; recommended best practice is to have least privilege roles for inference endpoints, and separate roles for billing/console access.
[22:18] Marta Ruiz: Is there an audit trail for who called which model and what parameters were used? We need provenance.
[22:26] Priya Nair: Yes, we provide request-level audit logs with request IDs, model version, timestamp, user/role, and non-content metadata. Note: request payloads can be included or excluded from logs depending on DLP settings and your contract.

[30:05] Evan Cole: Retention windows — what are the defaults, and how long can Redwood store logs? Also any options for export to customer SIEM?
[30:17] Priya Nair: Default operational logs are 90 days, audit logs 365 days in hosted. We offer extended retention as an add-on. Exports to S3 or direct ingestion to Splunk/Datadog via connectors are supported for enterprise plans.

[36:40] Sonal Patel: For the private option — VPC peering or on-prem — how isolated is the control plane? We need to show isolation to auditors.
[36:50] Jordan Lee: For Private deployment, you get a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. We provide network diagrams and architecture docs that auditors accept. We'll include those in the trust center.

[40:02] Marta Ruiz: About penetration testing reports — redacted summaries are fine. Do you accept shared attestations from third-party pentest vendors?
[40:11] Priya Nair: Yes, we include high-level pen test summaries internally and can provide redacted findings. For deeper verification, we can coordinate with our security team to allow auditor questions under NDA.

[45:30] Evan Cole: One tricky item: for SOC 2 evidence, our auditors want proof of key rotation event history. Is that granularly available, with timestamps and who rotated?
[45:44] Priya Nair: Key rotation events are logged with admin identity, timestamp, and key fingerprint. If you're using CMK we point to your KMS logs. We'll include sample log snippets in the materials.

[50:10] Jordan Lee: Quick recap: Jordan will send Trust Center link with SOC2 Type II, ISO cert, pen test summary. Priya will prep KMS slides and sample audit logs. Evan will map Tidewater controls and provide owners. Sonal will send IP allowlist for short POC.
[50:34] Marta Ruiz: That works. Can we get the trust center before Friday? We want to review before our internal compliance sync Monday.
[50:44] Jordan Lee: Yes targeting Thursday EOD, but we'll try for Wednesday. I'll mark the deliverable for Wednesday.

[55:12] Evan Cole: Couple more quick Qs — what's the SLA for evidence requests? A typical request might be 'show console screenshot of retention setting' — how fast can Redwood respond?
[55:25] Jordan Lee: For common artifacts we usually respond within 48 hours; for deeper evidence like bespoke logs it can be 3-5 business days depending on scope. We'll surface any blockers early.

[57:01] Marta Ruiz: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via the shared ticket and Jordan/Evan will coordinate offline on the mapping doc.
[57:10] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. Priya will send available slots for the KMS demo. Bye.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

NOTES: small transcription artifacts: sometimes "SCIM" transcribed as "skim", and "KV cache" appears as "K V cash" in older exported notes. Certain proper names may be slightly off in auto transcript.
